key_insight: ProIQA shifts math item quality assessment from stem-only checks to process-aware evaluation, using reasoning trees to judge items across knowledge, difficulty, and competencies.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a scalable way to screen automatically generated math problems for educational usefulness, making it relevant for AIG pipelines in intelligent tutoring and assessment systems.
method: Formulate IQA under three process-aware dimensions: knowledge concepts, difficulty, and disciplinary competencies.
Use LLMs to build hierarchical reasoning trees from raw solutions.
Encode tree structure with GNNs and fuse it with stem semantics in a dual-view “Stem + Solving” model.
evidence_signal: The paper reports extensive experiments on K12 math datasets showing that process-oriented features improve fine-grained assessment of AIG outputs.
watch_item: The approach depends on reliable solution-to-reasoning-tree construction, so errors from the LLM or noisy solutions could affect assessment quality.
paper_title: ProIQA: A Process-Based Framework for Fine-Grained Math Item Quality Assessment
